claim_formal: ∀ C>0 ∃ n ∃ f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} nonconstant: Σ_i f̂({i}) > C·√deg(f)

quote_A.text: For every real \(C>0\), there are a positive integer \(n\) and a nonconstant Boolean function

quote_B.text: We disprove the Gopalan–Servedio square-root conjecture, even up to an arbitrary constant factor.

notes: Family of counterexamples indexed by C. Conjecture also sits in O'Donnell's problem list (P3 alternative); treated as named conjecture. Construction sizes finite but unbounded ('we do not obtain useful bounds on their growth').

claim_formal: ∀ regular local R, ∀ nonzero f.g. M,N: (ℓ(M⊗N)<∞ ∧ dim M + dim N = dim R) → χ^R(M,N) > 0

quote_A.text: then \[ \chi^R(M,N)>0. \]

quote_B.text: We prove Serre's positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic.

notes: Paper footnote records a Dec 2025 public post (Editan/Copilot/Gemini) claiming the prime-quotient form, explicitly not treated as an established theorem, so not O9. Corollary: strict-transform multiplicity bound.

claim_formal: ∀ flat local homomorphism (R,m)→(S,n) of nonzero Noetherian local rings: e(R) ≤ e(S)

quote_A.text: Then \[ e(R)\leq e(S). \]

quote_B.text: We prove Lech's multiplicity conjecture

notes: Lean comparator DuttaDomain formalizes an intermediate lemma (Dutta multiplicity bound for complete local domains in char p), not Lech's inequality itself.

claim_formal: ∃ 3-dim complete Noetherian normal local domain R ⊇ ℂ with residue field ℂ such that no nonzero f.g. R-module has depth 3

quote_A.text: such that no nonzero finitely generated $R$-module has depth three

quote_B.text: This disproves the domain form of the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture.

notes: Lean comparator only asserts existence of a ring with the ambient properties (complete normal local domain, dim 3, residue field ℂ), not the absence of MCM modules. Hochster later expected counterexamples, but the conjecture is the posed statement. Corollary: affine-local (essentially finite type) counterexample; general obstruction K^2-2c_2 ≤ 6H^2.

claim_formal: ∃ finitely presented torsion-free G ∃ α,β ∈ F_2[G]\{0}: αβ = 0 (and G has a finite 2-dim classifying space)

quote_A.text: There exist a finitely presented torsion-free group \(G\) and nonzero elements \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb F_2[G]\) such that \(\alpha\beta=0\).

quote_B.text: We disprove Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture

notes: Also Problem 6 in Kaplansky's 1957 list (P3 alternative); coded P1 since posed and named as a conjecture.

claim_formal: ∃ finitely presented torsion-free G ∃ a,b,c ∈ F_2[G]: ab = 1 ∧ ac = 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 (hence ba ≠ 1)

quote_A.text: There exist a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ and elements $a,b,c\in\Ftwo[G]$ such that \[ ab=1,\qquad ac=0,\qquad c\ne0. \]

quote_B.text: We construct a finitely presented torsion-free counterexample to Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture over the field of two elements.

notes: Family also has: char-2 counterexample with odd torsion (finite field K), odd-characteristic counterexample (p from (m!)^2+1), Gottschalk surjunctivity refutation, and Determinant Conjecture refutation built on the char-2 companion. Lean comparators formalize the companion counterexamples (char 2 with odd-order torsion, f.g./f.p.; odd char; determinant), not the torsion-free F_2 headline, which they do not imply or follow from directly. The torsion-free paper adapts the construction of the OpenAI zero-divisor paper (family 196).

claim_formal: ∃ finite-dimensional unital ℂ-algebra A: ∀ m≥1 ∃ f.d. module N_m with 2m-2 ≤ pd N_m < ∞; hence findim A = ∞

quote_A.text: In particular, \(\findim A=\infty\).

quote_B.text: This disproves the little finitistic-dimension conjecture.

notes: Inner ∀m∃N_m is part of the witness property (findim A = ∞). Corollaries: big finitistic dimension infinite, injectives do not generate, extreme left-right asymmetry (second Lean comparator). An independent OpenAI companion (Tachikawa paper, family 199) also gives char-2 algebras with infinite findim.

claim_formal: ∃ k=F_2(q,H_1,H_2)-algebra Λ (f.d.) ∃ f.d. nonprojective Λ-module Z: ∀ i≥1 Ext^i(Z,Z) = Ext^i(Z,Λ) = 0 (stable under all field extensions)

quote_A.text: There exist a finite-dimensional $\kk$-algebra $\Lambda$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective left $\Lambda$-module $Z$ such that

quote_B.text: We disprove the Auslander–Reiten conjecture for Artin algebras.

notes: Family bundles refutations of Auslander–Reiten, Gorenstein-projective, Tachikawa's second conjecture (symmetric algebra; second Lean comparator), and via an endomorphism algebra the classical/generalized/strong Nakayama, Auslander–Gorenstein and Wakamatsu tilting conjectures, plus infinite finitistic dimension. Headline taken as Auslander–Reiten per summary order.

claim_formal: ∀ char-0 field F ∀ c≥1, 2≤a_1≤…≤a_c ∀ homogeneous I ⊆ F[x] containing a regular sequence of degrees a_i: ∃ lex-plus-powers ideal J with H_{S/J} = H_{S/I} ∧ β_{p,j}(S/I) ≤ β_{p,j}(S/J)

quote_A.text: For every homogeneous ideal containing such a sequence, the corresponding lex-plus-powers ideal has the same Hilbert function and at least as large a graded Betti number in every homological and internal degree.

quote_B.text: We prove the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field

notes: Matrix ambiguous: EGH is existence of a (lex-plus-powers) monomial ideal with the same Hilbert function (M2); the LPP Betti part is an inequality (M1). Coded O5 because the conjectures are posed over arbitrary fields and the result is char 0 only (tie-break 6); O1 is plausible if char 0 is considered the main case. Two manuscripts (EGH via commuting division-coefficient forms; LPP Betti theorem).

claim_formal: ∃ countable char-0 division ring D with center F ∃ x,y ∈ D: D = F[x,y] ∧ [D:F] = ∞ ∧ every element of D algebraic over F

quote_A.text: There is a countable division ring $D$ of characteristic zero

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the Kurosh problem for division rings.

notes: Counterexample to a universal question (tie-break 5). Kurosh's 1941 'Problem (K)' is a question, not a numbered problem database, so P2.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ finite group G ∀ p-block B of G: l(B) = |W_p(B)|

quote_A.text: For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$, and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$, \[ l(B)=|W_p(B)|. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every finite group and every prime p.

notes: Numerical identity between two counts per block; M7 (identity) vs M1 (property holds) is a judgment call. Corollaries: Alperin's local-global consequences and principal-block bounds.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ algebraically closed K of char p ∀ M≥1: {KGb : G finite, b block with |defect group| ≤ M} meets only finitely many K-linear Morita classes

quote_A.text: only finitely many \(K\)-linear Morita equivalence classes of \(KGb\) occur

quote_B.text: We prove Donovan's conjecture over every algebraically closed field K of characteristic p > 0.

notes: Finiteness statement with no bound given; coded M1 (property). Second manuscript proves the stronger integral form over W(F_p-bar) and any complete mixed-char DVR with alg. closed residue field. Coefficient descent cites the OpenAI blockwise Alperin weight paper (family 202). Donovan's conjecture also appears as Conjecture M in Alperin's 1980 problems account (P3 alternative).

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∀ dominant λ,μ,ν of Spin(2n) with λ+μ+ν ∈ Q(D_n) ∀ N≥1: (V(Nλ)⊗V(Nμ)⊗V(Nν))^G ≠ 0 → (V(λ)⊗V(μ)⊗V(ν))^G ≠ 0

quote_A.text: Then, for every positive integer $N$, \[ \bigl(V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\otimes V(\nu)\bigr)^G\ne0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow

quote_B.text: This resolves the type-D part of the simply-laced saturation conjecture.

notes: Theorem stated as ⇔ but one direction is trivial; content is the implication (saturation), so M1 rather than M5. Kapovich–Millson conjecture covers all simply-laced types; type A was known, type D is settled here, type E remains, hence O5.

quote_A.text: For every integer $m\ge1$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash N_m$, \[ g(\rho_m,\rho_m,\lambda)>0. \]

quote_B.text: This proves Saxl's conjecture.

notes: Companion manuscript also proves the Pak–Panova–Vallejo tensor square conjecture (∀ n∉{2,4,9} ∃ λ ⊢ n ∀ ν: g(λ,λ,ν)>0, a ∀∃∀ statement with Lean comparator UniversalTensorSquares) using the stronger cyclic Saxl statement; corollary on unipotent tensor squares of GL_n(F_q).

claim_formal: ∃ finite nonempty lattice L ∀ finite algebra A: L ≇ Con(A)

quote_A.text: There exists a finite nonempty lattice $L$ such that \[ L\not\cong\Con(A) \] for every finite nonempty algebra $A$ of every finite signature.

quote_B.text: In particular, the finite lattice representation problem has a negative answer.

notes: Prefix kept as ∃ with the ∀A inside the witness property (a strict prenex reading would be ∃∀). The other manuscript adds a colored-graph characterization (M5) and undecidability of representability and of full subgroup-interval recognition (M10); the title gives these equal weight, so M10 is a defensible alternative headline. Lean comparator formalizes the graph criterion (part i), a different result.

claim_formal: ∀ discrete group G ∀ q≥1 ∀ idempotent e ∈ M_q(ℓ^1(G)) ∃ finite F ⊆ C_fin(G): τ_C(e) = 0 ∀ C ∉ F

quote_A.text: There is a finite set $F\subset\mathcal C_{\rm fin}(G)$ such that $\tau_C(e)=0$ for every $C\notin F$.

quote_B.text: We prove the ℓ1-Bass conjecture for every discrete group.

notes: Inner ∃F is a finite-support property, not a main-object witness. Companion proves the complex group-ring Bass trace conjecture, the integral Bass conjecture and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture over char-0 domains for torsion-free groups. The ℓ1 paper builds on the OpenAI complex group-ring Bass paper. Lean comparators (BassTrace, BassTorsionFree; truncated in input) formalize the complex group-ring version, a special case of the ℓ1 headline.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ alg. closed k of char p ∀ finite symmetric tensor category C over k ∃ n≥1 ∃ fiber functor C → Ver_{p^n}(k)

quote_A.text: there are an integer $n\geq1$ and a fiber functor

quote_B.text: We prove the finite case of the Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture

notes: BEO Conjecture 1.4 concerns all symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth; only the finite case is proved (O5, tie-break 6). Corollaries: finite case of Coulembier–Etingof–Ostrik Conjecture B (classification of incompressible finite categories).

claim_formal: ∃ 2-dim ramified regular local ring A of mixed char (0,5) (explicitly A = (V[x,y]/(5+x^4+y^4))_(5,x,y)): ker(K_5(A) → K_5(Frac A)) ≠ 0

quote_A.text: Then $A$ is a Noetherian regular local domain of dimension two and \[ \ker\bigl(K_5(A)\longrightarrow K_5(\Frac A)\bigr)\ne0. \]

quote_B.text: This disproves Gersten's conjecture in its unrestricted integral form.

notes: Witness explicitly fixed; prefix ∃ per tie-break 1. Companion gives a K_3 counterexample at another ramified ring. The conjecture remains open for unramified rings, but the posed unrestricted integral form is refuted.

claim_formal: ∀ b≥6 ∀ f.d. complex V ∃ GL(V)-equivariant injection Sym^6(Sym^b V) ↪ Sym^b(Sym^6 V)

quote_A.text: there is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection \[ \Sym^6(\Sym^b V)\ \hookrightarrow\ \Sym^b(\Sym^6 V). \]

quote_B.text: We prove the sixth-symmetric-power case of Foulkes' conjecture.

notes: Equivalent to Schur-positivity of h_b[h_6]-h_6[h_b] (an M1 reading). O5: case a=6 of Foulkes' conjecture for all a. Uses the OpenAI companion (quadratic stabilization: canonical Foulkes–Howe map surjective for b ≥ a(a-1), which also answers Landsberg's Problem 7.19); the Lean comparator formalizes that companion result, so 'different'.

claim_formal: ∀ q∈(0,4]: FK(q) planar maps (V(M_n), a_n d_n, μ_n) →_law unit-area γ(q)-LQG sphere; ∀ q>4: (V(M_n), c(q) n^{-1/2} d_n, μ_n) →_law Brownian CRT (GHP)

quote_A.text: converge in Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov law to their ordinary unit-area Liouville quantum gravity spheres

quote_B.text: We resolve the finite spherical cases of Gwynne and Miller's graph-metric conjecture

notes: No matrix code fits scaling limits cleanly: coded M7 (identification of the limit object); M9 (threshold at q=4) is an alternative. O5 because the papers state the finite spherical cases of the Gwynne–Miller conjecture; q>4 CRT is a separate prediction settled in full. Random-walk/LBM and spectral results rely on companion and stated Brownian/LQG inputs. Lean FKCRT covers only the q>4 half.

claim_formal: ∀ nonatomic law G on [0,∞) with E[min(X_1..X_4)^2] < ∞: ℙ-a.s. planar FPP on Z^2 has no bigeodesic

quote_A.text: Then, with probability one, there is no sequence \((v_i)_{i\in\Z}\) of pairwise distinct vertices

quote_B.text: This resolves the planar no-bigeodesics conjecture under that moment assumption.

notes: O5: the conjecture is for all iid continuous laws; the moment-free formulation is explicitly not claimed. Second manuscript: exponential FPP limit shape strictly convex with C^1 boundary, differentiability for Gamma laws (resolves those conjectures for exponential weights). Lean comparators formalize the limit-shape results, not no-bigeodesics.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive G with p_c(G) < 1: P_{p_c}(∃ infinite open cluster) = 0

quote_A.text: If $\pc(G)<1$, then \[ \PP_{\pc(G)}(\text{there is an infinite open cluster})=0. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the bond form of the criticality conjecture of Benjamini and Schramm.

notes: Prefix: an almost-sure non-existence statement, read as ℙ per tie-break 4 (∀ with a probability-zero matrix is an alternative). O5 vs O1: the paper says it settles the 'bond form' (site percolation is more general via line graphs), so restricted class; O1 if the bond form is taken as the posed problem. Includes Z^d for all d; separate manuscript proves bond and site percolation on Z^3.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive G: p_c(G) < p_2→2(G) ≤ p_u(G)

quote_A.text: \qquad \pc(G)<\ptwo(G)\le\pu(G). \]

quote_B.text: We prove the bond-percolation nonuniqueness conjecture of Benjamini and Schramm

notes: Strict inequality between thresholds with no rate, so M1. Also proves Hutchcroft's operator-threshold conjecture, the critical triangle condition and mean-field exponents, and the Cayley-graph case. O5 vs O1: as in 213, only the bond form.

claim_formal: The 2D nearest-neighbour O(3) model has a canonical continuum limit as β→∞ (normalized by χ_β, ξ_β): it exists along all β, satisfies the OS axioms, is non-Gaussian, has a unique vacuum and a positive mass gap

quote_A.text: We construct a canonical interacting massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor $`O(3)`$ model

quote_B.text: Constructs the canonical continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor $`O(3)`$ model: a non-Gaussian local relativistic theory with a unique vacuum and a positive mass gap.

notes: Construction of a specific QFT; prefix 'none' (named model) vs ∃ (the limit exists) is debatable. The inputs name no specific conjecture for the O(3) construction (P2). Family also has the exact O(4) lattice mass asymptotic m ~ 32 e^{π/4-1/2} √β e^{-πβ} (M9), sharp O(4) mass bounds plus all-temperature gap, an isolated particle pole for the O(3) field (built on the companion prescription), and exponential decay for O(n), n≥3, at every β ('resolves the all-temperature exponential spin-decay conjecture'). The ClassicalON Lean comparator covers that last result, so 'different'.

claim_formal: For the square-lattice nearest-neighbour cosine XY model at b_c: C_{b_c}(r) = B r^{-1/4} (log r)^{1/8} (1+o(1)) as r→∞, with B ∈ (0,∞)

quote_B.text: Janke records the critical prediction, up to a multiplicative constant, as

notes: Problem is the Kosterlitz/BKT physics prediction rather than a formally named conjecture (P1 vs P2). Family also proves the BKT essential singularity √(b_c-b) log ξ(b) → A, the exponent 1/4, and discrete Gaussian height universality through the roughening threshold. The center-magnetization and critical spin-field results are conditional on stated companion inputs (height, renormalization, spin-field).

claim_formal: ∀ β>1: Var F_n(β) ~ c_β n^{1/3} with c_β > 0, and (F_n − E F_n)/sd(F_n) ⇒ ν_β (a unique nondegenerate law), for zero-field Gaussian SK

quote_A.text: We also prove that its variance divided by n1/3 converges to a finite positive constant.

quote_B.text: The one-sixth fluctuation prediction has a separate physics history.

notes: Physics prediction of the n^{1/6} scale (Kondor; Crisanti et al.): P1 vs P2. The companion paper proves sd = n^{1/6+o(1)}; the main paper adds the exact variance constant and a limiting law characterized by its moments, a stronger result than the predicted scale. Corollaries: SK–Curie–Weiss fluctuations, disorder-chaos bounds.

claim_formal: ∀ even finite-range square-symmetric potential V ∃ λ_0>0, β_c(λ), Z_σ(λ), Z_ε(λ): ∀ |λ|<λ_0 ∀ C^2 Jordan domain D ∀ boundary b: scaling limits of mixed spin/energy correlations = Z_σ^n Z_ε^m × nearest-neighbour Ising CFT correlations

quote_A.text: =Z_\sigma(\lambda)^nZ_\epsilon(\lambda)^m \mathcal C_D^b(\boldsymbol x;\boldsymbol y).

quote_B.text: We prove conformal universality of mixed bulk spin and energy correlations for the square-lattice Ising model with sufficiently small, square-symmetric, finite-range even multispin perturbations of either sign.

notes: Universality: the limit is identified with the nearest-neighbour Ising CFT up to field renormalizations (M7; M5 or 'other' also plausible). Physics universality predicts this for all finite-range ferromagnetic perturbations; only the weak-perturbation regime is treated, hence O5. The inputs name no specific conjecture (P2). Family also has SLE_3 interfaces for weak contour interactions and quenched SLE_3 for weak iid random bonds (later papers build on companions), plus log relative fluctuations conditional on stated reference estimates. Lean BufferedIsing formalizes a finite-graph comparison lemma.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3 ∀ E ∈ (−2√(d−1), 2√(d−1)): unfolded adjacency-eigenvalue point process of uniform random d-regular graph at E → GOE bulk process (Laplace functionals)

quote_A.text: the unfolded eigenvalue point process of the adjacency matrix of a uniform simple labelled d-regular graph converges to the GOE bulk process

quote_B.text: It proves the fixed-degree bulk-universality conjecture stated in \cite[Conjecture 2.11]{BourgadeHuang}

notes: Convergence to a named limit law coded M7, as for scaling limits generally (no better fit). Extension: fixed-energy GOE universality under weak iid uniform diagonal (Anderson) disorder, adapting the clean companion's arguments.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3 ∀ iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbour environment law μ on Z^d ∀ ℓ ≠ 0: P_0(X_n·ℓ → +∞) ∈ {0,1}

quote_B.text: We prove the directional zero–one conjecture for nearest-neighbor random walks in independent and identically distributed strictly elliptic environments on ℤd, d ≥ 3

notes: Annealed zero-one law: a deterministic statement about a probability, so prefix ∀ not ℙ. d=2 was known (Zerner–Merkl), so d≥3 completes the iid elliptic case (O1); O5 if the strict-ellipticity class is read as a restriction. Family also proves the zero-one law for finite-range-dependent uniformly elliptic environments, and Sznitman's ballisticity conjecture (directional transience ⇒ ballistic, d≥2, uniformly elliptic), with Lean comparators for both.

claim_formal: ∀ Poisson-diluted even-arity Ising model in the Panchenko–Talagrand class (first-moment integrability): lim_N F_N = inf_{r≥0} Φ_r

quote_A.text: the thermodynamic limit exists and \begin{equation}\label{main:formula} \lim_{N\to\infty}F_N=\inf_{r\ge0}\Phi_r. \end{equation}

quote_B.text: This resolves the equality conjecture stated immediately after Theorem~4 of Panchenko--Talagrand~\cite{PT04}, for their Poisson, even-arity Ising model class

notes: Exact variational value of the limiting pressure (M9). The PT conjecture is posed for exactly this class, so O1 (tie-break 6 exception), though the general Mézard–Parisi picture is broader. Corollaries: Viana–Bray, diluted even p-spin, soft even-K SAT, ground-state limits.

claim_formal: ∀ α>0 ∀ bounded Borel f: lim_N E p_N(f) = P_f(α) := inf_q {α V_f(q) + S_I(q)} and p_N(f) → P_f(α) in probability (Gaussian Ising perceptron); same for Gaussian spherical perceptron with bounded continuous potential

quote_A.text: Moreover, $p_N(f)$ converges to $\mathcal P_f(\alpha)$ in probability.

quote_B.text: We determine the limiting free energy of the Ising perceptron with independent Gaussian patterns for every bounded Borel log-potential, at every fixed positive temperature and pattern density.

notes: The inputs name no conjecture for finite-temperature perceptron free energies beyond physics replica predictions (P2 vs P1). Headline bundles Ising and spherical perceptrons; the PerceptronFreeEnergy Lean comparator covers only the spherical half (IsingFiniteness covers finiteness of the variational value), hence 'weaker'. Also: bi-orthogonally invariant spherical extension; negative spherical perceptron jamming threshold with exponents γ, θ (M9).
